findings.highlight: flees the castle with the black giant
findings.evidenceJa: 黒い巨人に連れられ
findings.governingReading: The girl escapes because the black giant carries or leads her from the castle.
findings.explanation: The English makes them merely flee together and weakens Berserker’s initiating protective agency.

findings.highlight: to run to the forest
findings.evidenceJa: 守りの薄い森へと逃れた
findings.governingReading: Illya leaves the best defensive site for the forest, where protection is thin.
findings.explanation: The English omits the defensive disadvantage that makes the flight paradoxical.

findings.highlight: The “enemy” is approaching the castle
findings.evidenceJa: “敵”がゆっくりと城に近づいてくる
findings.governingReading: The perceived enemy advances slowly toward the castle.
findings.explanation: The English omits the threatening deliberateness of its pace.

findings.highlight: suppressing her unease
findings.evidenceJa: 堪えきれない不安に蓋をした
findings.governingReading: Illya uses self-reassurance to put a lid on anxiety she cannot endure.
findings.explanation: The English weakens unbearable fear to unease and removes the containment image.

findings.highlight: Even the one with no reason left
findings.evidenceJa: 口を閉ざした筈の狂戦士でさえ
findings.governingReading: Even the Berserker who should have been mute conveys that she must flee.
findings.explanation: The English retains lost reason but omits the impossible communication that demonstrates independent protective agency.

findings.highlight: The thing that reached the outer wall
findings.evidenceJa: 城の外壁に手をかけたソレ
findings.governingReading: The entity places a hand on the castle’s outer wall before surmounting it.
findings.explanation: The English removes the embodied contact and staging.

findings.highlight: make their way through the forest
findings.evidenceJa: 森を[ruby text=はし o2o=1]疾走る
findings.governingReading: Berserker carries Illya at a sprint through the forest.
findings.explanation: The English removes speed and urgency.

findings.highlight: a withered magus
findings.evidenceJa: 枯れ木の如く老いた魔術師
findings.governingReading: The aged magus resembles a dead, withered tree.
findings.explanation: The English converts the simile into a generic adjective and loses the visual comparison.

findings.highlight: jumps to the ground
findings.evidenceJa: 黒い巨人から降り
findings.governingReading: Illya gets down from Berserker to confront Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English adds a jump and unnecessary athletic force.

findings.highlight: coldly glares at him
findings.evidenceJa: 冷淡な瞳で見つめる
findings.governingReading: Illya watches Zouken with cold, detached eyes.
findings.explanation: The English adds overt aggression to her controlled disdain.

findings.highlight: The plan was to take part in the next ritual
findings.evidenceJa: 次の儀式で行う筈じゃった
findings.governingReading: Zouken originally intended to carry out this plan in the next ritual.
findings.explanation: The English reduces his operational agency to merely participating.

findings.highlight: My earnest desire is about to come true
findings.evidenceJa: 悲願はあと一手で叶おうとしておる
findings.governingReading: Zouken claims his long-held wish is one move from fulfillment.
findings.explanation: The English omits the game-piece continuation and exact remaining step.

findings.highlight: go back to the pit where you belong
findings.evidenceJa: 大人しく地の底に戻ったら
findings.governingReading: Illya tells Zouken to return quietly beneath the earth.
findings.explanation: The English adds a moralizing “where you belong” absent from her dismissal.

findings.highlight: if I can seize you here
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=おまえ char=2]聖杯を押さえておけば
findings.governingReading: Zouken says securing the Grail—written with Illya as its reading—will make his plan unshakable.
findings.explanation: The English drops the written Grail layer and presents only seizure of Illya.

findings.highlight: My dearest wish is virtually complete
findings.evidenceJa: 我が悲願は磐石じゃ
findings.governingReading: Holding Illya would make Zouken’s long-held plan secure against failure.
findings.explanation: The English changes contingency insurance into near-completion.

findings.highlight: Hostility lights up in the old man
findings.evidenceJa: 老人に鬼気が灯る
findings.governingReading: A demonic or terrifying intensity ignites in Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the transformation to ordinary hostility.

findings.highlight: The white skull gets up, but stops in contrast to the old man’s wish
findings.evidenceJa: 白い髑髏がゆらりと立ち上がるも、老人の意思に反して動きを止めた
findings.governingReading: Assassin rises with an eerie sway, then halts contrary to his Master’s intention.
findings.explanation: The English loses the motion’s quality and renders the command conflict as an awkward contrast with a wish.

findings.highlight: immortality
findings.evidenceJa: 不老不死
findings.governingReading: Zouken desires both freedom from aging and death.
findings.explanation: The English preserves endless life but drops agelessness.

findings.highlight: Hatred shows in the girl’s eyes
findings.evidenceJa: 少女の瞳に嫌悪が宿る
findings.governingReading: Disgust appears in Illya’s eyes at the wish for immortality.
findings.explanation: The English changes revulsion into personal hatred.

findings.highlight: It rots by the second, reeking of decay, melts my flesh and bones
findings.evidenceJa: 刻一刻と機能を失い、悪臭を放ち、身体は内から溶け
findings.governingReading: Zouken says his body loses function moment by moment, emits a stench, and melts from within.
findings.explanation: The mature branch invents rot, decaying odor, and melting flesh and bones while losing the functional decline.

findings.highlight: my brain cells lose their knowledge
findings.evidenceJa: 脳細胞は蓄えた知識を失っていく
findings.governingReading: His brain cells progressively lose the knowledge they have stored.
findings.explanation: The English makes individual cells possess knowledge and omits accumulation and progressive loss.

findings.highlight: the pain of rotting alive
findings.evidenceJa: 生きながら崩れ行く苦しみ
findings.governingReading: Zouken describes the suffering of collapsing or disintegrating while still alive.
findings.explanation: The English narrows bodily dissolution to rot.

findings.highlight: If it’s painful, you can be at ease if you die
findings.evidenceJa: それに耐えられないなら消えればいい
findings.governingReading: Illya first says that if he cannot endure the price, he should disappear, then separately proposes death as relief.
findings.explanation: The English omits the first demand and collapses the sequence.

findings.highlight: You will never know what it means to be human
findings.evidenceJa: 人間には近づけなんだ
findings.governingReading: Zouken says the Einzbern dolls failed to draw near to humanity.
findings.explanation: The English changes an ontological failure into lack of understanding.

findings.highlight: laughs from the bottom of his heart
findings.evidenceJa: 心底おかしそうに哄笑
findings.governingReading: Zouken laughs loudly as though genuinely, profoundly amused.
findings.explanation: The English uses a sincerity idiom that does not convey amusement and sounds unnatural.

findings.highlight: like a mosquito bite
findings.evidenceJa: 蚊ほどのものでもない
findings.governingReading: Compared with death, Zouken says this pain does not amount even to something mosquito-sized.
findings.explanation: The English invents a bite and converts scale into a familiar pain comparison.

findings.highlight: like a pus in my brain
findings.evidenceJa: 蚊ほどのものでもない
findings.governingReading: The active source minimizes his current pain beside death with a mosquito-scale comparison.
findings.explanation: The mature branch invents pus in the brain and reverses the rhetorical image.

findings.highlight: an exception even within the humans
findings.evidenceJa: 人間の中でも特例
findings.governingReading: Illya calls Zouken an exceptional case even among human beings.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed.

findings.highlight: Do you want not to die that bad?
findings.evidenceJa: そんなに死にたくないの
findings.governingReading: Illya asks whether he is truly that desperate not to die.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed and blunts her cold challenge.

findings.highlight: I cannot die
findings.evidenceJa: ワシは死ぬ[ruby text=ワケ o2o=1]道理にはいかん
findings.governingReading: Zouken insists that he cannot allow himself to die or accept dying under this logic.
findings.explanation: The English turns compulsive refusal into literal incapacity.

findings.highlight: what conclusions you come to in your life
findings.evidenceJa: いかな真理、いかな境地に辿り着こうと
findings.governingReading: Zouken says no truth or spiritual state one reaches can overcome annihilation and the world’s end.
findings.explanation: The English replaces truth and attained state with ordinary conclusions over a lifetime.

findings.highlight: the collapse of your body
findings.evidenceJa: 自己の消滅
findings.governingReading: Zouken names annihilation of the self alongside the end of the world.
findings.explanation: The English narrows existential nonbeing to bodily collapse.

findings.highlight: even at the cost of the world itself
findings.evidenceJa: 何者をも、たとえ世界そのものを犠牲にしても
findings.governingReading: He claims humans will sacrifice anyone—up through the world itself—for reachable survival.
findings.explanation: The English retains the world extreme but omits willingness to sacrifice any individual.

findings.highlight: I would gladly kill everyone in the world
findings.evidenceJa: 世界中の人間を一人一人殺してまわっておる
findings.governingReading: Zouken says he would go around killing every person in the world one by one if it fulfilled his wish.
findings.explanation: The English adds pleasure and omits the methodical one-by-one image.

findings.highlight: prolong your life for a day
findings.evidenceJa: 僅か一日足らずの延命
findings.governingReading: Each tree would hypothetically extend life by less than a single day.
findings.explanation: The English raises the stated benefit to a full day.

findings.highlight: if the world dies because of your actions
findings.evidenceJa: その[ruby text=おこない char=2]伐採によって[ruby text=たにん char=2]世界が滅びようと
findings.governingReading: The line simultaneously names cutting as conduct and the world as other people: one would not care if that felling/action destroyed them/world.
findings.explanation: The English loses both written-reading pairings and their ethical argument.

findings.highlight: prospered, and nourished
findings.evidenceJa: 増え、肥満しきった有象無象
findings.governingReading: Zouken depicts humanity as proliferated, bloated, indiscriminate rabble.
findings.explanation: The English reverses grotesque overgrowth into positive prosperity and nourishment.

findings.highlight: There is no space for chain reaction now
findings.evidenceJa: 連鎖すべき法則など成り立たぬ
findings.governingReading: He claims no law capable of binding this human chain or collective still holds.
findings.explanation: The English mistakes social or causal linkage for a physical chain reaction and becomes incoherent.

findings.highlight: nobody will care even if I do not act in concert
findings.evidenceJa: ワシ一人が足並みを崩したところで誰にも異論は挟ませぬ
findings.governingReading: If collapse is inevitable, Zouken says no one may object when he alone breaks collective step.
findings.explanation: The English changes defiant self-exculpation into a prediction of indifference.

findings.highlight: I’m utterly amazed
findings.evidenceJa: あきれたわ
findings.governingReading: Illya responds with appalled exasperation at how far Makiri has lost sight of the purpose.
findings.explanation: The English changes condemnation into potentially admiring surprise.

findings.highlight: a voice not her own
findings.evidenceJa: 少女の声ではない声
findings.governingReading: The girl speaks in a voice unlike a young girl’s voice.
findings.explanation: The English falsely suggests the voice belongs to someone else or that Illya is possessed.

findings.highlight: particular about having human form
findings.evidenceJa: 人の身である事に拘り、人の身であるままに
findings.governingReading: They clung to being human and sought a beyond-human destination while remaining human.
findings.explanation: The English reduces existential human status to bodily shape.

findings.highlight: Justeaze’s mimicry
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=ユスティーツァ char=2]先祖の真似事
findings.governingReading: Zouken dismisses Illya’s speech as imitation of her ancestor, specified by the ruby as Justeaze.
findings.explanation: The English reverses possession and makes Justeaze the imitator.

findings.highlight: distorts his face in hatred
findings.evidenceJa: 醜悪に形相を歪め
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s features twist into a hideous expression as he glares.
findings.explanation: The English invents hatred as the emotion and drops the visual ugliness.

findings.highlight: the pressure on the girl increases
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=ふあん char=2]重圧が増大
findings.governingReading: The oppressive weight bearing down on Illya—read explicitly as anxiety—increases with the crawling shadow.
findings.explanation: The English omits both physical burden and the anxiety reading.

findings.highlight: the girl’s order
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=あるじ char=2]少女の命
findings.governingReading: Berserker enters battle without awaiting his master’s command, with girl as the written surface and master as its reading.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the event but loses the master-girl written relationship.
